title: molt upgrade reports a failed git pull as skipped, with a cause that cannot be true, and drops git's reason
body:
Found by critic-shell while reviewing the fix for issue 0013 on 16 Oct; not reproduced live.

`editors_upgrade` pulls the Doom config with `git pull --ff-only 2>/dev/null`, and on failure warns "Doom config pull skipped (not on tracking branch or already up-to-date)". `_upgrade_pull_repos` does the same for the framework and the user config repo. Two things are wrong with that:

- "already up-to-date" cannot be the cause. An up-to-date pull exits 0, so this branch only runs on a real failure.
- git's actual reason (no network, diverged history, local changes in the way) goes to /dev/null, and the upgrade carries on as if nothing happened. That is the issue 0013 shape: a failure reported as a skip, and the sleeve then called ready on a tree that was never updated.

Not fixed with 0013, because what an offline `molt upgrade` should do is a decision. It could stop, or run the hooks against the trees it has and fail at the end. The obvious fix: let git's stderr through, keep the warning only when there is no upstream (`git rev-parse --abbrev-ref '@{upstream}'` fails), and treat every other pull failure as a failure.


## Ruling (hv, 22 Oct 2026): run on, fail at the end

A pull that fails does not stop the upgrade and is not a skip. `molt upgrade` lets git's stderr through, runs the liberators against the trees on disk so the sleeve still settles what it can, counts the pull failure as a failure of the run, and ends non-zero without `Sleeve ready`, naming the repo whose pull failed. Only a repo with no upstream (`git rev-parse --abbrev-ref '@{upstream}'` fails) is a warning that the pull was skipped, and the run goes on as before. The same shape for the framework, the user config repo and the Doom config pull in `editors_upgrade`. cc builds on `issue-0015` after `issue-0016`; a pull that fails under test is faked, not real.


## As built (22 Oct 2026)

Merged to main as 7332c6b from issue-0015 b85fc84 (cc). `molt_git_pull` in `lib/molt.sh` pulls fast-forward only with git's output captured: a repo whose branch has no upstream configured warns that the pull was skipped and returns 2; any other failure is an error naming the repo, git's words indented under it on stderr, returning 1. "No upstream" is read from the branch's config, not from `git rev-parse @{upstream}`, which also fails for an upstream configured and gone; that pull is tried and fails with git's reason. `_upgrade_pull_repos` tries both repos, names each failed one in `_UPGRADE_FAILED_PULLS`, and the full upgrade runs every liberator's upgrade hook and the resleeve on the trees on disk, carrying the failed pulls through the restart a framework pull makes in `MOLT_UPGRADE_FAILED_PULLS`, then `_upgrade_finish` ends non-zero without `Sleeve ready`, naming the repos. `molt upgrade --self-only` ends non-zero on a failed pull. `editors_upgrade` uses the same pull, still runs doom sync, then fails the hook unless the pull updated or was skipped for want of an upstream. Tests fake the failing pull in `test/molt.bats` and `test/liberators/editors.bats`; the merged tree passed under brew bash and /bin/bash 3.2, shellcheck clean, and the branch's tests were red on main's code. CI run 39804805167 green.
